scope: alert person who can swallow with possible mild fluid loss after heat, exercise, vomiting, diarrhea, or poor intake; not a diagnosis
patterns: I have not been drinking enough today
my mouth is dry after being sick
what are mild signs of dehydration
my urine is darker than usual after exercise
my child has had fewer wet diapers
how can I replace fluids after diarrhea
I feel thirsty and tired after being outside
what should I give a vomiting child to drink
can I use oral rehydration solution at home
response: If the person is alert and can swallow, offer small, frequent sips of fluid. An oral rehydration solution can replace fluid and salts after vomiting or diarrhea; use a product prepared and given according to its label, especially for a child. Do not force a large drink at once if that triggers vomiting.
red_flags: marked sleepiness or being difficult to wake
very little or no urine, or very dark urine
unable to keep fluids down at all
a baby with sunken soft spot, dry mouth, no tears when crying, or fewer wet diapers
an older person becoming weaker or more confused
